To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of a systematic screening tool in the clinical setting can help identify patients with epilepsy who have depression and 2) the use of this tool is associated with increased patient satisfaction with the visit.
depression is a common and serious comorbidity in epilepsy and that it has a negative impact on quality of life and on the risk of seizure recurrence.

the use of a systematic screening approach to identify patients with epilepsy who have depressive symptoms is feasible and acceptable in a busy clinical practice and that the use of this approach is associated with a significant reduction in depressive symptoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of depression in patients with epilepsy in a busy outpatient clinic.
the identification of the most effective and efficient ways for clinicians to identify depression in people with epilepsy.
the development of a novel screening tool for depression in epilepsy that is brief, valid, reliable, and easy to administer in a busy clinical environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the prevalence of depressive disorder is high in patients with epilepsy, and it is more common than in the general population, and the prevalence is similar in men and women, but it is higher in patients who have a history of depression, and the presence of depression is a predictor of poor quality of life.
the presence of a depressive disorder is associated with increased risk of suicide attempts and death by suicide in patients with epilepsy.
the presence of a depressive disorder in epilepsy patients is associated with a higher rate of seizures, lower quality of life, and increased mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to use a simple and brief screening tool for depression in epilepsy in clinical practice.
the use of a structured depression screening instrument in epilepsy care enhances the recognition of depressive symptoms.
it is possible to identify depression in epilepsy patients in a busy clinical practice with a systematic depression screening tool.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a brief, systematic screening tool for depression in epilepsy is feasible and effective.
the use of an electronic health record (EHR)–based screening tool for depression in epilepsy patients can be effective in identifying depression and in improving depression care.
we need to do more to identify and manage depression in people with epilepsy (PWE).
